referents.why: qatal 'he had appointed for Pharaoh' in the relative clause on the frogs: the one who sent the frogs against Pharaoh is the LORD. Moses and Pharaoh are also masculine singular, but the act is God's

links.why: the order is going out (cl0), then crying out (cl1); this link runs backward
wayyiqtol: they went out, and then Moses cried out, on the narrative line
the relative clause 'which he had appointed for Pharaoh' sits inside the object of cl1, 'the matter of the frogs'; it fills the role of the noun it modifies
links.category: relative clause inside a noun phrase

cant_tell.what: whether Moses' cry (cl1) is the carrying out of Pharaoh's command 'pray to the LORD' (Exo.8.4 cl2)
cant_tell.why: the verb differs (cry out, not pray) and the report has no asah plus ken pro-form, which the fulfils form is defined by; the fit is plausible but the form does not settle it
